sections.label: Increase in licensed vets
sections.summary: The number of licensed vets has increased more than five-fold over two decades, reaching close to 700 by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Over the last two decades, the number of licensed vets has increased by more than five-fold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: There are close to 700 licensed vets as of end-2025.

sections.label: Vet Council establishment signalled
sections.summary: MND and NParks signalled in 2023 the move to establish a Vet Council to oversee professional matters for the vet sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Public expectations of professional standards and accountability have also risen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: And against this backdrop, the Ministry of National Development (MND) and the National Parks Board (NParks) had signalled the move to establish a Vet Council in 2023 to oversee professional matters for the vet sector.

sections.label: Extending regulation to vet professionals
sections.summary: Only vets must be registered at the outset, but regulation is planned to eventually extend to other veterinary professionals such as vet nurses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: While only vets are required to be registered at the outset, we plan to eventually extend regulation to other veterinary professionals, such as vet nurses who are currently not licensed, with an appropriate transition period to allow the sector to adjust.

sections.label: Existing vets deemed qualified
sections.summary: Existing vets holding a licence under the ABA will be temporarily deemed to be duly qualified vets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Existing vets holding a licence under the ABA will be temporarily deemed to be duly qualified vets.

sections.label: Vet nurses supervision and penalties
sections.summary: Clause 29 does not prohibit vet nurses from practising under supervision, and the Bill raises the maximum financial penalty to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For instance, clause 29 does not prohibit vet nurses from practising veterinary medicine so long as they act under the supervision of a duly qualified vet and in accordance with prescribed conditions, as they do today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Bill will raise the maximum financial penalty to $50,000 – a $4,000 increase compared to the current level of $10,000 provided under the ABA.

sections.label: Laypersons on committees
sections.summary: A Complaints Assessment Committee must include a layperson, and a Disciplinary Committee must include two laypersons to represent public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: A Complaints Assessment Committee must include a layperson, and a Disciplinary Committee must include two laypersons, namely a legal professional and an observer, to represent public interest and ensure accountability.

sections.label: Disciplinary and interim orders powers
sections.summary: Clause 56 lets the Disciplinary Committee cancel or suspend a vet's registration and fine up to $50,000, while clause 66 lets the Interim Orders Committee suspend or restrict registration for up to 18 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For more egregious cases of misconduct or negligence, clause 56 empowers the Disciplinary Committee to take stronger disciplinary action against a vet, including cancelling or suspending a vet's registration or practising certificate, and imposing a penalty of up to $50,000, which is aligned with that for the human healthcare professions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As these inquiries may take time, clause 66 empowers the Interim Orders Committee to either suspend or impose conditions or restrictions on a vet's registration for a period not exceeding 18 months while disciplinary proceedings are ongoing.

sections.label: Appeals and Council regulations
sections.summary: The General Division of the High Court hears appeals against the Committees' orders, and Part 6 lets the Council make regulations on registration qualifications, continuing professional education and professional standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The General Division of the High Court will hear appeals against the Disciplinary Committee or the Interim Orders Committee's orders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Lastly, Part 6 of the Bill provides powers for the Council to make regulations on qualifications for registration, continuing professional education requirements and professional standards.

sections.label: Strengthening veterinary professional standards
sections.summary: As the pet population grows and vet care becomes more complex, the Bill strengthens professional standards, clarifies regulated vet services and establishes a disciplinary framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As the pet population in Singapore grows and as vet care becomes more complex, it is right that we strengthen professional standards, clarify the scope of regulated vet services and put in place a robust disciplinary framework.

sections.label: Affordable animal care policy objective
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MND and AVS make clear, affordable and accessible animal care part of the policy objective in implementing the framework, including standards, codes and requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: My suggestion, therefore, is that MND and AVS make clear and affordable and accessible animal care be an important part of the policy objective in how this framework is implemented, including the development of standards, codes and requirements over time.

sections.label: Tracking veterinary care costs
sections.summary: The speaker encourages AVS to begin tracking broad trends in the cost of veterinary care and share this regularly with the Committee and the Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Third, I would encourage AVS to begin tracking broad trends in the cost of veterinary care and to share this regularly with the Committee and the Council.

sections.label: Affordability and accessibility of pet care
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the sector is observed before wider regulation, and that MND and AVS examine the broader cost of animal care so it stays affordable and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But I hope we at least first observe how the establishment of the Veterinary Council affects the sector, especially in terms of manpower, service delivery and cost, before extending regulation more widely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And finally, I hope that MND and AVS initiate a serious effort to examine the broader cost of caring for animals in Singapore, to ensure that care remains affordable and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Many residents, volunteers and animal lovers active within my constituency of Kebun Baru, including myself, would be happy to contribute to such an engagement on affordable and accessible pet care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But as we professionalise the sector, let us keep faith with the ordinary pet owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Let us make sure that the better standards do not come at the cost of accessibility, and affordability remains a central and real consideration in how this new framework is implemented.

sections.label: Veterinarian registration framework tiers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a three-tiered registration framework for veterinarians based on qualifications: full, restricted and specialist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new three-tiered registration framework for veterinarians based on one's qualifications, namely full, restricted and specialist.

sections.label: Pets per vet ratio
sections.summary: The Singapore Veterinary Association states there were approximately 898 pets per vet as of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Veterinary Association, there are approximately 898 pets per vet as of 2022.

sections.label: Number of licensed veterinarians
sections.summary: As of September 2025, Singapore had approximately 674 licensed veterinarians, rising to around 700 by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As of September 2025, Singapore had approximately 674 licensed veterinarians, rising to around 700 by end-2025.

sections.label: Overseas students returning to practice
sections.summary: Among Singaporean veterinary students studying overseas, only 50% or less return home to practice, many preferring Australia or the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Amongst the Singaporean veterinary students that study overseas, which comprise an overwhelming majority, only 50% or less choose to return home to practice, as many prefer to work in Australia or the UK, where opportunities abound, with perhaps better work life balance.

sections.label: Veterinary nursing graduates retention
sections.summary: The Singapore Veterinary Association states only 20% of veterinary nursing graduates remain in the industry after five years as of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Veterinary Association, only 20% of veterinary nursing graduates remain in the industry after five years, as of 2022, with many of them viewing this profession as unviable.

sections.label: Animal harm cases and CCTV review
sections.summary: NParks investigated 54 cases of harm to animals involving pet groomers over three years, and MND said the ABA review would consider CCTV requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A Parliamentary reply this year revealed that NParks investigated 54 cases of harm to animals involving pet groomers over the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Following questions raised in this House, MND indicated in January 2026 that the ABA review would consider whether to include the requirements for closed circuit television recordings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, two employees of a dog-training firm were suspended in 2024 for physically harming two dogs under their care in preparation for a photo opportunity.

sections.label: Strengthening veterinary profession and animal care
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to strengthen the veterinary pipeline, address brain drain, recognise professionals, enhance consumer protection, and tighten enforcement for pet groomers and trainers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope we can do more by strengthening the pipeline of veterinary professionals, plugging the brain drain faced by the industry, recognising the contributions of our veterinary professionals, enhancing consumer protection measures within the industry, and tightening the enforcement regime for pet groomers and trainers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will nurture a driving animal care ecosystem that is centred around the health and welfare of its patients, whether it is domesticated pets, community animals or the wildlife in our garden city.

sections.label: Blurred distinction in veterinary landscape
sections.summary: The blurred distinction between specialised and non-specialised treatment in a GP-heavy veterinary landscape creates a need for deeper regulation, and the proposed three-tiered system's robustness is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This blurred distinction between specialised and non-specialised treatment in the current "GP-heavy" veterinary landscape creates a need for deeper regulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, we must ask if the proposed three-tiered system is sufficiently robust.

sections.label: Specialist tier requirements in subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry will substantiate the specific requirements for the specialist tier in the subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, will the Ministry substantiate the specific requirements for the specialist tier in the subsidiary legislation?

sections.label: Interim Order suspending vets
sections.summary: Under clause 56 of the Bill, an Interim Order can suspend a vet for up to 18 months while investigations proceed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, under clause 56 of the Bill, an Interim Order can suspend a vet for up to 18 months while investigations proceed.

sections.label: Abuse gap for veterinarians
sections.summary: The speaker raises the abuse gap, noting UK and Australian veterinary associations reported a surge in cyberbullying and physical intimidation by pet owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, we must talk about the "abuse gap." In the UK and Australia, the British and Australian Veterinary Associations have reported a surge in "cyberbullying" and physical intimidation by pet owners.

sections.label: Extending Industry Abuse Protections to veterinarians
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry will consider extending Industry Abuse Protections to veterinarians under the Vet Council, similar to the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons in the UK.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider extending the "Industry Abuse Protections" to veterinarians under the Vet Council, similar to the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons in the UK, to provide them with better occupational support?

sections.label: Veterinary specialist requirements and training grants
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify specialist veterinary category requirements and consider training support and grants for vets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For this reason, I would like to ask the Minister: First, will the Minister further clarify the specific requirements for the specialist veterinary category in subsidiary legislation?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, to complement the Bill and encourage more stringent and continuous professional development, will the Government consider providing training support and grants for vets?

sections.label: Manpower shortage and industry abuse protections
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether veterinarians will get Industry Abuse Protections like those of the UK Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The cost of manpower shortage will ultimately be passed on to consumers, as fewer veterinarians mean not only higher costs but also reduced choices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would also like to ask the Minister whether consideration will be given to providing veterinarians with "Industry Abuse Protections" similar to those established by the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons in the UK, to strengthen occupational safeguards for veterinary practitioners?

sections.label: Veterinary Council and licensed veterinarian numbers
sections.summary: The passage states the Veterinary Council, registration framework and disciplinary proceedings are overdue, with over 690 licensed veterinarians, up almost five-and-a-half-folds since 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The establishment of the Veterinary Council, the creation of proper registration framework and the introduction of disciplinary proceedings are long overdue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There are currently over 690 licensed veterinarians which has increased almost five-and-a-half-folds since 2006, serving an ever-growing population of pet owners who rightly expect professional, accountable care for their animals.

sections.label: Penalty for unqualified veterinary practice
sections.summary: Clause 29(6) makes unqualified practice an offence punishable by a fine up to $50,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 29(6) makes unqualified practice an offence punishable by a fine of up to $50,000 and imprisonment of up to 12 months.

sections.label: Enforcement resources for Bill implementation
sections.summary: The passage asks what additional enforcement resources the Government intends to allocate to support the Bill's implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, what additional enforcement resources does the Government intend to allocate to support the implementation of this Bill?

sections.label: Non-veterinarian acts and excluded acts
sections.summary: Clause 29(5) allows non-veterinarians to perform certain acts under veterinarian supervision, while clause 29(7) reserves diagnosis, surgery, drug prescription and certificates for veterinarians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Some of the activities currently performed by community animal caregivers could, on a broad reading, fall within this definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 29(5) allows non-veterinarians to perform certain acts within the practice of veterinary medicine, provided these acts are not excluded acts and are performed under the supervision of a duly qualified veterinarian and in accordance with prescribed conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The excluded acts defined in clause 29(7), which include diagnosis, surgery, drug prescription and the issuance of professional certificates are strictly reserved for veterinarians.

sections.label: Engagement and enforcement transition
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will engage animal welfare organisations and community caregivers in developing subsidiary regulations, and whether there will be a transition period before enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, will the Government engage the animal welfare organisations and community caregivers in developing the subsidiary regulations under this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, will there be a transition period during which enforcement action is not taken against bona fide community caregivers performing basic first aid?

sections.label: Licensed veterinarian numbers
sections.summary: NParks noted Singapore had over 690 licensed veterinarians in October 2025, five and a half times more than in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: NParks noted during public consultations that Singapore has over 690 licensed veterinarians in October 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is five and a half times more than the number in 2006.

sections.label: Melbourne DVM tuition fees
sections.summary: The University of Melbourne's international DVM tuition fee is nearly A$86,000 per year as of 2026, meaning $300,000 or more to complete the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The University of Melbourne's international tuition fee for DVM is nearly A$86,000 per year as of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This means a student would typically have to pay $300,000 or more in tuition fees to be able to complete this concurrent degree programme.

sections.label: Veterinary study grants and scholarship
sections.summary: NParks' Study Grants Programme supports Singapore Citizens in full-time overseas veterinary programmes, and the NParks-Peter Lim Scholarship supports less privileged youths in veterinary and animal science careers.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: NParks' Study Grants Programme supports Singapore Citizens pursuing a full-time veterinary programme in an accredited overseas university, and also NParks-Peter Lim Scholarship explicitly supports less privileged youths pursuing careers in the veterinary and animal science sector.

sections.label: Veterinary technology and animal care pathways
sections.summary: Temasek Polytechnic offers a diploma in veterinary technology listed as a full-time agrifood and animal care pathway, while ITE publicly offers shorter or part-time animal care and grooming courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, Temasek Polytechnic already offers a diploma in veterinary technology and Singapore Food Agency's sector career page lists that this particular diploma, it is a full-time pathway into a broader agrifood and animal care space.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, at the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) level, I realise that the publicly visible offering seems to be shorter courses or part-time animal care and grooming programmes, such as basic aquatic animal care, with a course duration of seven hours, and a certificate of competency in dog care and grooming with a duration of 14 hours.

sections.label: Structured pathways and veterinary nurses
sections.summary: If the response is no or not yet, the speaker hopes the Government will consider more structured pathways, noting NParks said the Veterinary Council will regulate veterinary nurses in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the response is no or not yet, then I hope the Government will consider more structured pathways to be developed over time, especially since NParks have already said in the longer term, the Veterinary Council will also regulate veterinary nurses, which will play an important role in supporting animal care.

sections.label: Penalties and professional benchmarks
sections.summary: NParks says the framework drew on healthcare, built environment and overseas veterinary regimes, and the Bill carries a $50,000 fine and/or 12 months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: NParks has said that this framework has developed with reference from professional regimes in healthcare and the built environment, as well as overseas veterinary statutory boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is reassuring, especially because the Bill itself says that for unauthorised practice and related misconduct also carry significant penalties of a $50,000 fine and/or up to 12 months of imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, I would like to clarify how the MND arrived at this, and what benchmark were they using to determine this?

sections.label: Independence of appeal processes
sections.summary: Appeals routed to the Minister or decisions across stages involving the same bodies may raise questions about how independent the processes are perceived to be.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, if a certain appeal is routed to the Minister, or where decisions are made across different stages that involves the same bodies, there may be questions about how independent and clearly separated the processes are perceived to be.

sections.label: Pathways to becoming animal doctor
sections.summary: Getting this right would let a young Singaporean pursue becoming an animal doctor through clear pathways, not family income.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If we get this right, then I will be also able to say to a young Singaporean that if your dream, your aspiration is to be an animal doctor, there are clear pathways and structures for you to get there; and for you to achieve this aspiration, it is never a function of your family's income.

sections.label: Support for Veterinary Council formation
sections.summary: Because interventions may be ineffective even when everything possible is done, the speaker supports forming the Veterinary Council, the focus of Part 2.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, other times, they may have done everything possible, but the interventions were simply ineffective.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is why I support the formation of the Veterinary Council, the principal focus of Part 2 of the Bill.

sections.label: Layperson representation on Council
sections.summary: NParks says public consultation raised broader representation suggestions; Clause 4(3B) stipulates two laypersons but it is unclear how informed they would be about consumer affairs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to NParks, the public consultation accompanying the Bill did raise suggestions for broader representation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 4(3B) does stipulate that two individuals should be laypersons, but it is unclear how informed these members would be about consumer affairs.

sections.label: Resident's authenticity verification allegation
sections.summary: A resident alleged that a key document submitted to AVS for investigation did not appear to be independently verified for authenticity, suggesting the prior regime fell short.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I say this in part because, based on the experience of at least one of my residents, the prior regime may have fallen short.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That resident has alleged that a key document submitted to AVS for investigation did not appear to be independently verified for authenticity.

sections.label: Animal cruelty cases and ABA review
sections.summary: The speaker cites reported cat abuse cases and falling confirmed cruelty cases, and asks when the Animal and Birds Act review will conclude and a Bill be debated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Recent events, such as the well reported cases of abuse of cats at Everton Park and Punggol, and the throwing of cats off high floors, hinted the disturbing rise in recorded cases of cruelty inflicted on animals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, even as confirmed cases fell, from 961 in 2024, to 608 last year, the absolute number is not befitting of an educated populace and advanced society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I understand that MND is undertaking a review of the ABA, which was last amended in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry be willing to share when this review is expected to conclude and when we might expect a Bill to be debated in this House?

sections.label: Veterinary Council and professional standards
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a Veterinary Council, strengthens registration, requires continuing professional education and sets up a disciplinary framework to build trust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, if we want to build trust, we must make sure what they see is clear, consistent and credible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That is why the direction of this Bill is the right one – establishing a Veterinary Council, strengthening registration, requiring continuing professional education and putting in place a clear disciplinary framework.

sections.label: Pricing transparency in veterinary sector
sections.summary: Pricing sits outside the Bill's scope, but clearer communication, better upfront estimates and a more consistent sector approach would strengthen transparency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While pricing may sit outside the scope of this Bill, transparency is something we can strengthen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clearer communication, better upfront estimates and a more consistent approach across the sector would go a long way.

sections.label: Structuring the wider ecosystem
sections.summary: Better outcomes require thinking ahead in structuring the wider ecosystem with clear roles, standards and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we want better outcomes, then we must think ahead in how we structure this wider ecosystem, with clear roles, clear standards and clear accountability.

sections.label: Elected members on Medical and Dental Councils
sections.summary: The Medical Council has 12 elected members out of 27 and the Dental Council five out of 13, by statute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Medical Council and the Dental Council both have, by statute, elected members from the profession – 12 out of 27 for the Medical Council and five out of 13 for the Dental Council.

sections.label: Smaller practices and Council rules
sections.summary: Smaller practices will likely bear a heavier burden from future Council rules than chains like Mars Veterinary Health, which runs at least 19 of Singapore's 121 licensed vet centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, smaller practices will likely bear a heavier burden from future Council rules than chains like Mars Veterinary Health, which runs at least 19 out of Singapore's 121 licensed vet centres, about one in six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 87(3) states, "Regulations made under this Act may make different provisions or prescribe different fees for different classes of persons or different circumstances", and all regulations require the Minister's approval under sections 87(1) and 87(2).

sections.label: ASEAN veterinary accreditation gap
sections.summary: No ASEAN veterinary degree programme holds accreditation from the American, Royal College or Australasian bodies that permit practice in those regions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: No veterinary degree programme in any Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member state currently holds accreditation from the American Veterinary Medical Association, the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons or the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council – the three bodies whose recognition permits practice in North America, the UK and Europe and Australasia, respectively.

sections.label: Veterinary compensation fund proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an industry-wide pooled compensation fund as a last resort for pet owners when a veterinarian's negligence causes loss and insurance is inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Some may even believe they are adequately covered, only later to discover the exclusions and limitations or when the treatments become absolutely necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: So, while educating the public about pet insurance is vital, I propose a more comprehensive approach: do consider the establishment of a compensation fund, potentially pooled across the profession.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This fund could serve as a crucial safety net in serious cases where a veterinarian's negligence results in loss, where insurance proves inadequate, unavailable or has lapsed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For instance, the legal profession has a compensation fund and the Motor Insurers' Bureau of Singapore provides compensation for victims of uninsured or untraceable drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I believe the veterinary sector should explore a similar industry-wide pooled fund as a last resort, ensuring that pet owners are not left without a practical remedy when unforeseen and severe circumstances arise.

sections.label: Overseas veterinary study demand
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government has studied demand for veterinary studies in Singapore and how many local students study overseas each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Studying overseas is costly and this may put the profession out of reach for capable Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: So, I ask the Ministry whether the Government has done a study on the demand for the studies in Singapore and how many local students each year have to study overseas if they want to become vets.

sections.label: Legal professional on Interim Orders Committee
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Interim Orders Committee suspend or restrict a vet up to 18 months, but the speaker says a legal professional should sit on it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The Bill allows the Interim Orders Committee to suspend or restrict a vet for up to 18 months even before the disciplinary matter is finally decided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Yet, unlike the Disciplinary Committee, there does not appear to be a requirement for a legal professional to sit on the Interim Orders Committee itself.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Where powers of this seriousness are exercised, it would be good to have a legal professional on the Interim Orders Committee to provide safeguards against procedures and substantive irregularities and errors and to uphold rules of fairness and procedural justice during disciplinary proceedings for vets.

sections.label: Declaring pro bono hours
sections.summary: The speaker suggests veterinarians declare pro bono hours during annual licence renewal or as part of continuing professional education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: One practical step could involve veterinarians declaring their pro bono hours during their annual licence renewal or consider this as part of the continuing professional education.

sections.label: Resident's document authenticity allegation
sections.summary: The Member said a resident alleged that key documents submitted to AVS for investigation did not appear to be independently verified for authenticity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Member had said that, I quote, "Based on the experience of at least one of my residents, the prior regime may have fallen short and that the resident had alleged that the key documents submitted to AVS for investigation did not appear to be independently verified for authenticity.

sections.label: Public trust in procedure
sections.summary: The speaker says she represented the case and did not insinuate lapses by AVS, but stresses public trust in procedure is important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: To be clear, I represented her case and I also said in my speech that I was not insinuating whether there were any lapses in her case or not, by AVS.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But the point I was trying to make, and I will repeat it here, is that public trust and confidence in procedure is really important.

sections.label: Checking AVS correspondence, substantiating allegations
sections.summary: The speaker says they will check with AVS and any correspondence, and must substantiate allegations to uphold public trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Indeed, we will go back and check with AVS and any correspondence between the Member representing your resident and ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: At the same time, we will have to substantiate any of these allegations to ensure that public trust is upheld, of course, with AVS as well as other public institutions.

sections.label: Veterinarian and pet cat numbers
sections.summary: Consultation materials note over 690 licensed veterinarians as of October 2025, 1,000 to 1,500 veterinary nurses and technicians, about 41,000 licensed pet cats and over 41,500 course completions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Official consultation materials note that 690 over licensed veterinarians as of October 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Beyond veterinarians, there are around 1,000 to 1,500 veterinary nurses and technicians in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Since the cat management framework began on 1 September 2024, about 41,000 pet cats have been licensed, and over 41,500 people completed the online pet ownership course required for first-time applicants.

sections.label: Bill excludes pricing and fees
sections.summary: NParks has been clear that the Bill does not cover pricing and fees matters, and separate measures may be considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: NParks has also been clear that this Bill or the scope of this Bill does not cover pricing and fees matters and that separate measures may be considered to address these concerns.

sections.label: AVS and Veterinary Council roles
sections.summary: Consultation materials state AVS continues to regulate veterinary clinics and animal-related businesses and remains first responder for animal feedback, while the Veterinary Council regulates professional standards; the speaker supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The consultation materials make clear that AVS would continue to regulate veterinary clinics and animal-related businesses and remains the first responder for animal feedback, while the Veterinary Council itself will regulate professional standards for veterinary practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This division of responsibility should help the public know where to go to and help the sector operate with greater clarity, purpose and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: With these observations, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, offered in the spirit of strengthening the implementation and preserving trust, I support the Veterinary Practice Bill.

sections.label: Bill's regulatory objectives
sections.summary: The Bill aims to establish a more systematic regulatory system, stipulates that only qualified registered veterinarians may diagnose, operate, prescribe or issue certificates, and sets up a complaints and disciplinary mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The core objective of this Bill is to establish a more systematic regulatory system for the veterinary profession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the Bill clearly stipulates that only qualified registered veterinarians may conduct diagnoses, surgeries, prescribe medications or issue medical certificates, thereby ensuring the professionalism and safety of animal medical services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Bill also establishes a complete complaints and disciplinary mechanism, providing the public with clear channels to lodge complaints and obtain resolution when encountering professional issues.

sections.label: Veterinary Practice Bill framework
sections.summary: The Veterinary Practice Bill establishes the Veterinary Council, registration and practising certificate standards, and a complaints and disciplinary process to strengthen veterinary regulation and public confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill is proposed precisely against such a social backdrop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It not only improves the institutional foundation of the veterinary profession but also establishes a more solid framework for the healthy development of Singapore's pet medical industry in future. : In summary, the Veterinary Practice Bill provides a much-needed framework to strengthen the regulation and professional standards of veterinary practice in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This shift in social attitudes means that the public rightly expects a high level of professionalism, accountability and trust in veterinary services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill helps meet that expectation by establishing the Veterinary Council, setting clear standards for registration and practising certificates, and putting in place a structured process to address complaints and disciplinary matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In doing so, it strengthens both public confidence and the integrity of the veterinary profession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Do we have a sufficient pipeline of veterinary talent for the future?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: How can we better help pet owners understand the system and identify duly qualified veterinarians?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And as the sector continues to grow and specialise, how can we balance professional advancement with accessibility, transparency and trust?

sections.label: Licensed veterinarians and pet population
sections.summary: Licensed veterinarians in Singapore grew from 122 in 2006 to 674 as of September last year, with an estimated pet population of about 700,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The number of licensed veterinarians in Singapore has grown significantly from just 122 in 2006 to 674 as of September last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We have an estimated pet population of about 700,000, including some 114,000 dogs and 94,000 cats, with about one in three households now owning a pet.

sections.label: SPCA adoptions and rescues
sections.summary: SPCA adoptions fell from 979 in 2019 to 250 last year, while rescues rose from 2,813 in 2023 to 3,763 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Adoption rates at the SPCA have decreased sharply, from 979 in 2019 to just 250 last year, while rescues have climbed from 2,813 in 2023 to 3,763 last year.

sections.label: Vet fees and pricing transparency
sections.summary: Given vet fees rose up to 20% between 2022 and 2023 and the Bill may add compliance costs, the passage asks whether pricing transparency and informed consent on costs will be made statutory obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Given that vet fees rose by up to 20% between 2022 and 2023, and that this Bill may add further compliance costs, will the Ministry therefore consider making pricing transparency and informed consent on costs a statutory obligation under the Bill?

sections.label: Transition to professional regulatory framework
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill marks a transition from a licensing regime to a professional regulatory framework, recognising the veterinary sector's growth in scale, complexity and public expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We expect care that is modern, professional and accountable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It marks an important transition from a licensing regime to a professional regulatory framework, recognising that the veterinary sector has grown in scale, complexity and public expectations.

sections.label: Hospitalisation and emergency care costs
sections.summary: Hospitalisation can cost hundreds of dollars a night and emergency care can easily exceed $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hospitalisation can cost hundreds of dollars a night and emergency care can easily exceed $500.

sections.label: Veterinary fees outside Bill
sections.summary: Veterinary fees fall outside the scope of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Yet, veterinary fees fall outside the scope of this Bill.

sections.label: High-risk procedures not excluded
sections.summary: High-risk procedures such as anaesthesia administration are not excluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Importantly, high-risk procedures, such as the administration of anaesthesia are not excluded.

sections.label: Public checks doctor registration
sections.summary: The public can check a doctor's registration type, specialist branch, practising certificate status and active conditions or restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The public can check a doctor's registration type, specialist branch, practising certificate status and active conditions or restrictions.

sections.label: Bill disciplinary process safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a structured disciplinary process with safeguards like layperson involvement and conflict-of-interest rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill establishes a structured disciplinary process with safeguards like layperson involvement and conflict-of-interest rules.

sections.label: Limitation period and service timelines
sections.summary: The Bill sets a three-year limitation period, and asks what indicative service timelines are for triage, inquiry and final decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the Bill sets a three-year limitation period, what are the indicative service timelines for triage, inquiry and final decision?

sections.label: Vet registration fees
sections.summary: Asks what fees are required for vets to obtain and maintain their registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the fees required for vets to obtain and maintain their registration?

sections.label: Establishment of Veterinary Council
sections.summary: The establishment of a Veterinary Council is described as an important step forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In this context, the establishment of a Veterinary Council is an important step forward.

sections.label: Framework for vet nurses
sections.summary: Plans to develop a more formal framework for vet nurses and technicians in Singapore are noted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am glad to note from the Minister of State's opening speech that there are plans to develop a more formal framework for vet nurses and technicians in Singapore.

sections.label: Consumer protection in vet care
sections.summary: Recent reforms emphasised consumer protection, and AVS is called on to consider similar measures such as fee disclosures and itemised bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Recent reforms there have placed strong emphasis on consumer protection, including requiring clinics to publish price lists for common treatments, disclose ownership structures and strengthen complaints and redress mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The rationale is clear: vet care is a complex service, and consumers need better information to make informed decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to call on AVS to consider similar measures, such as clear fee disclosures for common services, provision of estimates for higher-cost procedures and more consistent itemisation of bills.

sections.label: Public access to practitioner information
sections.summary: Canada and Hong Kong make disciplinary outcomes and practitioner information publicly accessible, and Western Australia includes a consumer representative on its board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In jurisdictions, such as Canada and Hong Kong, disciplinary outcomes and practitioner information are made publicly accessible to varying degrees, enabling consumers to make more informed choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In addition, Western Australia's model includes a consumer representative within its Veterinary Practice Board, helping to ensure that public-interest considerations are incorporated into regulatory decision-making.

sections.label: Complaints resolved through education
sections.summary: Canadian data shows many complaints are resolved through advice, remediation or education, and a holistic approach is urged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: For example, data from Canada shows that many complaints are resolved through advice, remediation or education, rather than disciplinary sanctions alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This is particularly important in a manpower-constrained sector, where we must retain and support skilled professionals while at the same time, upholding standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, as we raise standards for veterinarians, we must also take a holistic approach, one that uplifts all members of the vet care team, strengthens workforce pipelines and local pathways and, at the same time, enhances consumer protection, transparency and trust.

sections.label: Duties of the Council
sections.summary: Its primary duty is to register vets, set practice standards and appoint disciplinary bodies to safeguard animal health and public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Its primary duty is to register vets, set and maintain high standards for the practice of veterinary medicine in Singapore and appoint necessary bodies for disciplinary proceedings to safeguard animal health and welfare as well as the public interest.

sections.label: Council vet composition requirements
sections.summary: The Council must include at least four other vets, one with at least 10 cumulative years of experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In this regard and to respond to Mr Kenneth Tiong's question, the Council must also comprise at least four other vets, including one with at least 10 cumulative years of experience as a vet, which may include the duration licensed by AVS or registered with the Council.

sections.label: Council layperson composition
sections.summary: The Bill requires the Council to comprise at least two laypersons who are non-vets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On Mr David Hoe and Mr Melvin Yong's queries, the Bill provides that the Council must comprise at least two laypersons who are non-vets.

sections.label: Vet registration and practising certificate
sections.summary: Every vet practising veterinary medicine must be registered with the Council and hold a valid practising certificate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Every vet that practises veterinary medicine must be registered with the Council and have a valid practising certificate.

sections.label: Maximum fine for unlawful practice
sections.summary: The Bill raises the maximum fine for unlawful practice or misrepresentation from $10,000 to $50,000, with no change to the 12-month imprisonment term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Compared to what is provided for under the ABA, this Bill raises the maximum fine for offences relating to unlawful practice of vet medicine or misrepresentation as a vet from $10,000 to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This is to provide sufficient deterrence against profit-driven motives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: There is no change to the existing 12-month maximum imprisonment term, and the $50,000 fine quantum is benchmarked against the human healthcare sector, including the dental and allied healthcare professions.

sections.label: Disciplinary inquiry completion timelines
sections.summary: Clauses 48 and 54 require the Complaints Assessment Committee and Disciplinary Committee to complete inquiries within three and six months respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's question about the completion timeline for the disciplinary inquiry, clauses 48 and 54 provide that the Complaints Assessment Committee and the Disciplinary Committee must complete its inquiry by three months and six months respectively.

sections.label: Complaint writing and statutory declaration
sections.summary: Any member of the public may complain against vets, but every complaint must be in writing and supported by a statutory declaration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, while any member of the public may submit a complaint against vets, every complaint must be made in writing and also supported by a statutory declaration.

sections.label: Minister approval and disciplinary safeguards
sections.summary: The Minister's approval is required for Council regulations, and disciplinary proceedings include safeguards for impartiality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Minister's approval must be sought when the Council makes regulations, such as those relating to qualifications and continuing professional education requirements for registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I also want to assure Mr David Hoe and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that the disciplinary proceedings likewise incorporate multiple safeguards to mitigate conflict of interest and to ensure impartiality.

sections.label: Appeals to Minister or High Court
sections.summary: Aggrieved parties may appeal to the Minister or the General Division of the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Third, aggrieved parties may also appeal to the Minister or the General Division of the High Court.

sections.label: Publishing disciplinary findings
sections.summary: The Council will publish disciplinary findings of key cases to raise standards and educate the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Council will also publish disciplinary findings of key cases when concluded, to facilitate awareness and uplift standards within the vet sector and for public education.

sections.label: Reviewing ethics code and costs
sections.summary: AVS will partner the Council to review the Code of Ethics and study suggestions for more transparent cost structures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, AVS will partner the Council to review the Code of Ethics and will study Members' suggestions for cost structures to be more transparent, such as to provide itemisation of bills and clearer fee disclosures.

sections.label: Pet ownership as personal choice
sections.summary: Pet ownership is a personal choice and long-term commitment with responsibilities, despite concerns about vet costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: While we understand that many Singaporeans see pets as a member of their family, mine included, and we understand concerns around vet costs, we must also recognise that pet ownership is a personal choice and a long-term commitment that comes with responsibilities.

sections.label: Vet representation and malpractice powers
sections.summary: The Bill gives the vet sector fair representation on the Veterinary Council, which can deal with malpractice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Under this Bill, there will be fair and adequate representation of the vet sector in the Veterinary Council to drive the refinement of professional services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Veterinary Council will also be equipped to effectively deal with malpractice to safeguard animal health and welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Kenneth Tiong, do you have a clarification arising out of the Minister of State's speech?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: So, can I just ask the Minister of State to clarify why vet representation is not codified on a statutory basis, unlike the Medical Registration Act of 1997 and the Dental Registration Act of 1999?

sections.label: NParks lean budget
sections.summary: NParks operates on a very lean budget and its staff handle many things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Basically, NParks is operating on a very, very lean budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: I have a lot of respect for NParks staff, but they have to handle a lot of things.

sections.label: Manpower and vet representation
sections.summary: Manpower projections and resource requirements are being studied, and vet representation on the Veterinary Council is codified in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, we are looking at manpower projections as well as resource requirements to study a local programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In fact, the vet representation on the Veterinary Council is already codified in the Bill.
